title: The Missing Baryons Census
bottleneck: Only about half of the baryons predicted by BBN and the CMB are accounted for in stars, cold gas, and hot cluster gas; the rest are believed to hide in the warm-hot intergalactic medium (WHIM). Detections via fast-radio-burst dispersion and X-ray absorption are accumulating but remain sparse and model-dependent. The warm-hot intergalactic medium is too diffuse to image directly and too cool to emit strongly, making it observable only in absorption or stacking.
why_it_blocks: An incomplete baryon census leaves galaxy formation's fuel supply and feedback energetics uncalibrated.
current_state: FRB dispersion measures and stacked SZ signals are closing the gap; a complete census is expected this decade but not yet in hand. Next-generation X-ray missions like Athena should detect WHIM emission lines and complete the census.
